# Digital filtering: moving average and IIR: the exercise

<!-- Generated by tools/maintainer/build_exercise_readmes.py from the lesson page. Edit the lesson, then run the script. -->

Lesson: [Digital filtering: moving average and IIR](https://jouhis.github.io/embedded-course/lessons/0107-digital-filtering.html). Read it first: the steps below refer to its diagrams and worked examples.

## Try it: the Pico filter on a noisy reading

The Wokwi potentiometer is perfectly steady, so the simulator shows no noise, and the project `projects/0107-filter-pico` therefore adds a seeded pseudo-random noise of about ±16 codes and a spike of 600 codes on every 25th sample, printing one CSV row per sample with the time, raw, median, moving average and EMA values. The first printed line is `FILTER OK`, the second the header `ms,raw,median,ma8,ema`, and a row follows every 50 ms.

1. Copy your finished `ma_update`, `ema_update` and `median3_update` from the host project into `projects/0107-filter-pico/starter/filters.c`, keeping the init functions already there.
2. In `starter/main.c`, replace the three placeholder lines `m = raw`, `a = raw` and `e = raw`, running `median3_update` on `raw` first and then passing the median output to both `ma_update` and `ema_update`, so that the two smoothers run side by side on the same de-spiked signal, which the CSV columns compare, exactly as the reference solution does and as the starter's comment describes as a chain.
3. Print `FILTER OK` once before the loop starts, as the reference solution does, although the starter's comment asks for it after the eight-sample window fills, either version printing the text the automatic check looks for.
4. Build with <kbd>Ctrl</kbd>+<kbd>Shift</kbd>+<kbd>B</kbd>, then <kbd>F1</kbd> → *Wokwi: Start Simulator*, and the serial monitor should show `FILTER OK`, the header and rows every 50 ms, the spike rows at 1250 ms and 2500 ms having a `raw` column about 600 codes higher than their neighbours while their `median`, `ma8` and `ema` columns barely move. The 0 ms row is the exception, because the median has no full window at start-up and passes its first inputs through, so the spike shows in the `median` column on that first row.
5. Copy the CSV from the serial monitor into a file and plot the columns, or paste it into a spreadsheet, and to see what the spike does to an average, change one line in `main.c` so that `ma_update` takes `raw` instead of `m`, rebuild and look at `ma8`, which now rises by about 75 codes for eight rows after each spike, because 600 ÷ 8 = 75, then change the line back before going on.

The reference solution, which prints `FILTER OK` and the CSV header first, is in `projects/0107-filter-pico/solution`.
